 Dhiraj Singh—Bloomberg/Getty Images With the world’s fastest-growing major economy, India’s government sees AI as critical to the country’s continued development. Sarvam AI, a Bengaluru-based startup co-founded by Pratyush Kumar, is close to the center of that effort, building AI tools trained on Indian languages as well as local data and cultural contexts. In June, it raised $234 million and was valued at $1.5 billion.
 Sarvam builds both underlying models—which the company says outperform some American rivals on selected India-focused benchmarks—and enterprise products for banking, government services, defense, and more. In June, it said its conversational-AI platform was handling over 2 million interactions a day. Sarvam has also partnered with several state governments on local computing infrastructure, research, and AI adoption.
 Kumar brings experience from his days as a researcher at Microsoft and IBM, and also co-founded AI4Bharat, an open-source Indian-language AI initiative. India, he wrote online in June, “cannot rent intelligence. We have to build it ourselves.”
